# E06 - Intraday strategies on XTIUSD / XNGUSD CFDs (Oanda 1-minute mids, 2005-01 .. 2020-05)

*Generated by `experiments/e06_intraday_summary.py` (numbers below are pulled from the result CSVs).*

## Bottom line

* **1288 strategy variants** were backtested (5 families x 2 instruments, parameters chosen on 2005-2012 only). After realistic CFD costs almost everything is dead. Most families have positive *gross* edge, but spreads and slippage eat it. Natural gas's 20 bp round trip kills every NG idea.
* **Only one idea is worth paper trading: WTI intraday momentum into the settlement.** At 14:00 NY, trade 14:00->14:30 in the direction of the move from the prior session's 14:30 to today's 09:30, and only when that move is in the top quintile of its trailing-year distribution. It scores net Sharpe IS 0.88 / OOS 0.53 / full 0.68 with 55 trades/yr and 9.4 bp net per trade. The predictability is real (Newey-West t = 3.6 IS, 2.5 OOS). The trading edge is thin, though. It halves at 2x costs (full 0.25), and it comes from high-volatility trending years: OOS without 2020 it is 0.21, and 2017-2019 lost money. The deflated Sharpe is low (DSR 0.10 on its own 44-trial family). Verdict: **marginal+ / promising only as a small, cost-sensitive satellite**. It is not a stand-alone bot.
* Opening-range breakout, EIA reaction, session drifts and short-term mean reversion: **reject** (details and the few marginal survivors below).
* The EIA releases matter for **risk management**, not alpha. The first minute after the crude report moves 5.2x a normal minute, and after the NG storage report 8.1x. 45% of NG storage releases move NG > 1% within 5 minutes.

## Setup

* Data: Oanda WTICO_USD / NATGAS_USD 1-minute **mid** candles, restructured into CME-style sessions (18:00 NY prior day -> 17:59 NY). The trading calendar is the full NYMEX sessions derived from the liquid WTI feed. Exchange holidays and early-close days are dropped, as a bot knows them in advance. That leaves ~250 sessions/yr and 3,848 sessions in total.
* Execution (no look-ahead): signals use the last close strictly before the decision time. Market orders fill at the open of the next bar. Resting stop orders are simulated on each minute's OHLC path (O->L->H->C if the bar closed up, else O->H->L->C). A gap through a level fills at the bar open.
* Costs per round trip: 2 x COST_PER_SIDE (XTI 3 bp/side, XNG 10 bp/side), plus STOP_SLIPPAGE (1 / 3 bp) per stop-type side. Entries or exits within 15 minutes after an EIA release are charged as stop-type (wide event spreads). Overnight holds pay 2.5%/yr / 365 per calendar night. Cost sensitivity is shown at 0x / 1x / 2x.
* P&L: 1x notional per trade. The daily series covers all sessions (zeros on no-trade days), annualised with 252. IS = 2005-2012 and OOS = 2013-2020-05. Parameters are picked on IS net Sharpe only.
* Trials: 1288 non-degenerate variants. By family and instrument (XTI/XNG): A ORB 486/486, B momentum 44/44, C EIA 50/50, D sessions 32/32, E mean reversion 32/32. Eight 15-minute Bollinger variants with a 1-hour window are excluded as degenerate: with n = 4 bars, |z| <= 1.5 < threshold. Descriptive scans (hourly/session/day-of-week t-stats, regressions) are extra looks that are not counted.
* Deflated Sharpe (Bailey & Lopez de Prado): `dsr_is_family` tests the IS Sharpe of the chosen configuration against the IS Sharpes of all trials in its family and instrument, which is where the selection happened. `dsr_full_global` tests the full-period Sharpe against all 1288 trials. The DSR treats cross-trial dispersion as noise, so it is conservative (cost-driven dispersion inflates the hurdle `sr0`).

## Data problems found (and how they were handled)

1. **Pre-Globex hours, 2005 to Jun 2006.** No quotes 09:30-10:00 NY (all of 2005, 43% of 2006 sessions) and none 14:30-15:15. These are the NYMEX ACCESS pauses around the pit session. Handled: price-at-time looks back at most 20 minutes, so the 10:00 predictors are NaN in 2005. 14:30 exits fall back to the 14:29 close.
2. **The pit open was at 10:00 NY until early 2007, then 09:00.** The 09:00 volatility spike appears only from Feb-Mar 2007, with |r| at 09:00 vs midday 0.38x in 2005 against 1.93x in 2010. So '09:00-anchored' rules in 2005-06 are not anchored to the real open. This hurts the ORB IS period.
3. **Microstructure noise, 2005-2006.** Quotes are coarse (median |dP| 0.050 USD on WTI in 2005) and 1-minute returns show lag-1 autocorrelation of -0.15 (2005) and -0.11 (2006), against about -0.02 later. This would flatter very short-horizon mean reversion. Even so, the 5-15 minute fades lost money gross in those years.
4. **The EIA releases register at 10:35, not 10:30, from Jun to Dec 2008,** for both reports and both CFDs, while the 09:00 open and 14:28 settlement spikes are on time. This is a feed or release quirk, not a clock shift. Handled in `ix.eia_schedule` (`results/e06_data_checks_eia2008.csv`).
5. **Holiday-week crude reports** came out Thursday 10:30 until Sep 2008 and Thursday 11:00 from Oct 2008, verified on the 1-minute spikes. With this rule the spike-at-scheduled-minute hit rate is 0.61 regular / 0.56 shifted. The NG storage report is Thursday 10:30 (hit rate 0.72), and weeks with a Tue-Fri federal holiday are dropped.
6. **Early-close / holiday sessions** (MLK, Presidents, Memorial, July 4, Labor Day, Thanksgiving + Friday, Christmas and New Year eves) have no 14:30 settlement in the feed. They are excluded via the calendar, since they are known in advance.
7. **Sparse NG quotes.** Only 68-78% of minutes 09:00-14:30 have an NG bar in 2013-2019, and overnight is far sparser. Missing minutes mean an unchanged mid, so prices are forward-filled for signals and fills wait for the next quote. There are no contract-roll jumps in the 17:00-18:00 break (large break gaps are post-holiday gaps). Note that the roll-yield part of a real broker swap is not in this price series; this matters only for the overnight holds.

## Family details and verdicts

### A. Opening-range breakout: **reject**

* Grid: anchor 08:00/09:00/09:30, N = 15/30/60 min, exit 14:30/16:55, stop none / opposite edge / midpoint, one reversal optional, filters none / narrow range (<1.0 or <0.75 of the 20-day average) / prior-day trend / both, plus the Crabel 'stretch' version that Holmberg, Lonnbark & Lundstrom (2013) tested (k = 0.5/1/2 x the 10-day average min(H-O, O-L)). That makes 486 variants per instrument.
* Gross edge exists: 92% of WTI variants have positive OOS *gross* Sharpe, consistent with the futures literature. After costs only 12% are positive, and 0% for NG.
* The canonical 09:00 / 30-minute range / 14:30 exit / no stop scores WTI net Sharpe IS -0.09, OOS -0.46, gross OOS 0.17, at 4.0 bp gross per trade against a 6-8 bp cost. The IS-best WTI version (Crabel stretch k = 0.5 from 09:00, hold to 16:55) scores IS 0.40 / OOS 0.17, with 3.3 bp net per trade, and is negative at 2x costs (-0.33). The IS-best classic-range version flips from 0.33 IS to -0.33 OOS.
* Conclusion: Holmberg et al.'s ORB profits in crude futures do not survive CFD costs out of sample. The gross edge is about 5-10 bp per trade and the cost is 6-8 bp (breakout entries pay stop slippage).

* The overnight-plus-first-half-hour return predicts the last half hour in both instruments, with the same sign IS and OOS. The 09:00->09:30 and 13:30->14:00 returns alone do not. Most of the WTI effect sits in 14:25-14:28, just before the 14:28-14:30 settlement window, and partly reverses at 14:30-14:35 (see `e06_B_momentum_regressions.csv`).
* Trading every day loses after costs (WTI `on930|all` net Sharpe -0.13, gross 1.18). The edge is concentrated in the strongest-signal days (chart `e06_momentum_buckets.png`): the top quintile earns about 17 bp gross in both IS and OOS, against a 6 bp round trip.
* IS-best WTI rule `on930|q0.8|14:30`: trade only when |signal| > the trailing-250-day 80th percentile. It scores IS 0.88 / OOS 0.53 / full 0.68, gross full 1.12, with 55 trades/yr, 9.4 bp net/trade, hit rate 0.52, max DD -20%, ann. return 5.1% at 7.5% vol (1x notional). The neighbours (on1000, q = 0.67, exit 14:28) are all positive OOS, so the parameter surface is smooth.
* Robustness (`e06_B_momentum_robustness.csv`):
  * entry 14:01: IS 0.91 / OOS 0.57 / full 0.72 (2013-16 1.11, 2017-20 0.32)
  * entry 14:02: IS 0.94 / OOS 0.60 / full 0.74 (2013-16 0.94, 2017-20 0.46)
  * exit 14:29 (early): IS 0.84 / OOS 0.61 / full 0.71 (2013-16 1.10, 2017-20 0.41)
  * exit 14:31 (late): IS 0.81 / OOS 0.37 / full 0.57 (2013-16 0.77, 2017-20 0.18)
  * long trades only: IS 0.85 / OOS 0.40 / full 0.59 (2013-16 1.11, 2017-20 0.18)
  * short trades only: IS 0.41 / OOS 0.34 / full 0.38 (2013-16 0.40, 2017-20 0.32)
  * EIA report days only: IS 0.20 / OOS 0.31 / full 0.26 (2013-16 0.45, 2017-20 0.21)
  * non-EIA days only: IS 0.86 / OOS 0.43 / full 0.63 (2013-16 0.88, 2017-20 0.28)
  * ex-2008: IS 0.45 / OOS 0.53 / full 0.49 (2013-16 0.97, 2017-20 0.34)
  * ex-2020: IS 0.88 / OOS 0.20 / full 0.61 (2013-16 0.97, 2017-20 -1.18)
  * vol-targeted size (cap 3x): IS 0.64 / OOS -0.03 / full 0.30 (2013-16 0.69, 2017-20 -0.70)
* Reading: this is genuine predictability, but a thin and regime-dependent trading edge. Profits come from volatile trending years (2007-09, 2014-16, 2020), and calm years (2012-13, 2017-19) bleed. Vol-targeting makes it *worse*, because the edge lives in high-vol days. Exiting one minute late (14:31) costs about 2 bp. At 2x costs the full Sharpe is 0.25. The breakeven cost is about 7.7 bp per side.
* NG: the same predictability exists (gross Sharpe up to ~1.3), but about 10 bp gross per trade cannot pay a 20 bp round trip. Every NG variant is negative OOS net (IS-best `mom|on1000|q0.8|14:30` scores OOS -1.30).

* The 30 minutes before the crude report are *quieter* than normal (ratio 0.78). The full 09:00-14:30 session is only 1.13x normal for WTI, but 1.35x for NG on storage days. The crude report barely moves NG, and the storage report barely moves WTI.

For WTI, the IS-best fade scores 0.37 IS and -0.65 OOS, and continuation is about zero even gross. The first-minute reaction is unpredictable in sign, and it is already in the price before a retail order can fill.
* NG continuation (w = 15 min, k = 2, hold to 14:30) scores IS 0.36 / OOS 0.36, but on only 9 trades/yr (t = 1.36, DSR ~0). That is marginal at best: too few events to distinguish from luck.
* The NG pre-report drift (short 09:00->10:29 on storage days) looked strong IS (0.69) and failed OOS (-1.12). It was NG's 2005-12 bear market in the morning hours, not a report effect: the same window on non-report Thursdays drifts the same way.

Sessions: Asia 18:00-02:00, London 02:00-08:00, NY pre 08:00-09:00, NY main 09:00-14:30, post 14:30-17:00. Overnight = prior 14:30 -> 09:00 (so overnight + NY main is the full settlement-to-settlement return).

* WTI: no session drift keeps its sign and significance from IS to OOS. The overnight/intraday split is flat (overnight 0.4 bp/day, intraday -2.4 bp/day, both insignificant). The best session hold loses after the 6 bp daily round trip.
* NG: the post-settlement drift is strong and persistent (+11.8 bp IS, t 8.9; +5.2 bp OOS, t 4.3; positive in 15 of 16 years; spread through 14:35-16:30, not a jump). It may be a feed artifact of thin afternoon quoting. Either way, ~9 bp/day against a 20 bp round trip is untradeable. NG's 2005-2020 decline happened mostly in NY hours: 09:00-14:30 averaged -7.3 bp/day.
* Day of week: the one notable cell is NG on Thursdays (storage day), 09:00-14:30 at -47 bp IS (t -3.0) and -27 bp OOS (t -2.3). As a rule (short NG every Thursday 09:00-14:30) it scores IS 0.49 / OOS 0.14, with years like 2016 at -34%. It is a bet that NG's secular decline continues on report days. Marginal/reject, and dangerous in an NG bull market. WTI Mondays (close-to-close) averaged -31 bp (t -3.0), almost all OOS and driven by weekend gaps in 2014-2020.
* Sunday gap: Friday 17:00 -> Sunday 18:00 reopen gaps have a standard deviation of about 158 bp (both instruments). For WTI, gaps tend to partially reverse by Monday 09:00 (slope t -5.8). The IS-best rule (fade gaps > 0.5% from 18:05 Sunday to 09:00 Monday) scores IS 0.11 / OOS 1.01, but on ~7 trades/yr, and OOS ex-2020 it is 0.91. Four March-April 2020 trades make up most of the OOS P&L. It is a curiosity, not a strategy: Sunday-open spreads are wide and stops gap through.
* Walk-forward session picker (each year hold the session with the largest trailing-3-year gross |t| if |t| > 2, in its sign, re-picked yearly): WTI OOS net 0.05. NG picks the post-settlement long almost every year, yet OOS net is -3.88 after costs (gross OOS 1.27). Picks are in `e06_D_walkforward_picks.csv`.

### E. Short-term mean reversion: **reject (no edge even before costs)**

* Fades of 5- and 15-minute z-score extremes (return z vs the prior 1 h / 4 h, or Bollinger z; |z| > 2 or 3), exiting at the rolling mean or after 30 minutes, plus VWAP-deviation fades: 32 valid variants per instrument. Only 25% of WTI variants are positive OOS *gross*, and the median OOS gross Sharpe is -0.30. At 5-15 minute horizons oil shows slight continuation, not reversion. After costs the best WTI variant is -0.55 OOS, and high-turnover variants reach Sharpe -3 to -8. Costs are decisive, as expected, and there was nothing to be decisive about.

## What a bot would need (if you take the WTI momentum rule to paper trading)

* **Signal (computed at 14:00:00 NY):** s = ln(P_09:30 / P_settle,prev), where P_settle,prev is the prior session's price at 14:29-14:30 NY and P_09:30 is the last mid before 09:30 NY. Keep a rolling 250-session history of |s|. Trade only if |s| > its 80th percentile, which gives about 55 trades/yr.
* **Orders:** a market order at 14:00-14:02 NY in sign(s), then a market exit at 14:29-14:30 NY. Do not hold past 14:30: 14:30-14:35 partially reverses (t = -4.8 on WTI). Delaying the entry by 1-2 minutes is harmless, but a late exit costs ~2 bp. Use no stop, or only a wide catastrophe stop (e.g., 3x the trailing 30-minute RMS); the tests used none.
* **Filters and calendar:** skip exchange holidays, early-close days and days with no 14:30 settlement. Use DST-aware NY time, not broker server time. Everything is flat by 14:30, so there is no swap.
* **Costs:** the edge is ~15 bp gross per trade and breaks even at ~7.7 bp per side. Only run it where the WTI CFD spread plus slippage at 14:00 and 14:30 NY is <= 3 bp per side, and measure the realised fills. Do not run it on XNGUSD.
* **Sizing and risk:** fixed notional per trade (vol-targeting hurt). Expect long flat or losing stretches in calm years (2012-13, 2017-19). Use a kill-switch on realised slippage rather than on P&L, and treat it as a small satellite, not a core strategy.

## Risk-management facts every intraday bot on these CFDs should encode

* **EIA crude report (Wed 10:30 NY; holiday weeks Thu 11:00):** WTI's first minute is ~5x normal size, the 99th-percentile 5-minute move is 2.5%, and 14% of reports move > 1% in 5 minutes. Recommendation: no new entries from 10:25 to 10:45, and move or widen stops, since stops placed near the market get gapped.
* **EIA natural-gas storage report (Thu 10:30 NY):** NG's first minute is ~8x normal, the 99th-percentile 5-minute move is 5.2%, and 45% of reports move > 1% within 5 minutes. Treat it as a scheduled gap event.
* **Settlement (14:28-14:30 NY)** is the high-volume closing range. Prices drift in the direction of the day into 14:28 and partially revert at 14:30-14:35.
* **Sunday reopen (18:00 NY):** weekend-gap standard deviation is about 158 bp, with 2020 examples of -33% (WTI 2020-03-09). Be flat over weekends, or size for gaps.
* **Holidays / early closes:** Globex halts at ~13:30 NY on MLK, Presidents', Memorial, July 4, Labor and Thanksgiving days, with no settlement. Any 14:30-exit logic must handle this.
